content: Tiered blockstore read path (miss -> remote fetch -> verify -> serve -> re-cache) matches IPFS node/gateway practice: local cache first, content-addressed verification of fetched bytes against the CID before publication, atomic insert into local cache, pinning to protect from GC, and GC deleting only unpinned data. IPFS persistence docs frame storage as finite: nodes must evict cached resources (garbage collection) and pinning gives explicit control over disk space and retention; pinning services and Filecoin provide the durable back tier with slower retrieval. Negative-result discipline (authoritative NotFound vs transport failure) is standard gateway practice per the repo architecture doc.
